enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (name, school, parents, family background etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **a)** "After receiving a phone call, my mother started jumping happily and shouting..." Continue the story.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Start with the given sentence and show the surprise of the family.
2. Explain the background: my mother's hard life as a farmer and the long wait for news.
3. The content of the phone call and the joy in the house.
4. The neighbours' reaction and the celebration.
5. The lesson: hard work and patience are rewarded.

**Model composition (459 words)**

After receiving a phone call, my mother started jumping happily and shouting, "Thank God! Thank God! My prayers have been answered!" I had never seen her behave like that before, and my little sister and I stood at the kitchen door with our mouths wide open, wondering whether she had lost her mind.

My mother, Mama Nkeng, is a poor farmer in our village. Since the death of my father five years ago, she had worked alone on our small farm to pay our school fees and to feed the family. Every morning, she woke up at five o'clock, carried her hoe to the farm and returned in the evening, tired and covered with dust. Many times, she went to bed hungry so that we could eat. Despite all this, she never complained, and she kept telling us that God would one day wipe away our tears.

Three months earlier, she had joined a farmers' cooperative and applied for a loan to buy fertilizer and good seeds. The wait had been long, and some women of the village had laughed at her, saying that such loans were only for rich people. My mother simply smiled and continued her work.

Now she was dancing in the courtyard. When she finally calmed down, she held us tightly in her arms and explained between laughs and tears. The caller was the president of the cooperative, who had announced that her application had been accepted. Not only would she receive the loan, but she had also been chosen as the best farmer of the year in our division. She would receive a prize of two hundred thousand francs and a new water pump for her farm.

I could not believe my ears. I jumped with joy as well, and my sister began to sing a song of thanks. Within a few minutes, the news had spread like bush fire, and the neighbours came running to our house. Those who had laughed at her before were the first to arrive, and they begged her to forgive them. My mother welcomed everybody warmly. In the evening, we cooked a big pot of rice and chicken, and the whole quarter ate and danced until late at night.

That night, before I fell asleep, I thought about everything I had seen. My mother's tears of sorrow had finally become tears of joy. She had never given up, even when everybody doubted her, and her patience had been rewarded. I promised myself that I would study very hard so that one day I would repay her sacrifices.

From that day, I understood that hard work, faith and patience always bring success, however long we may wait. My mother's shouting that evening is a sound I will never forget.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that continue the story from the given sentence, developed with details, in clear paragraphs with a beginning, a middle and an end |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Not starting with (or not linking to) the given sentence, so the story does not continue it.
2. A story with no clear ending or with a sudden change of tense between past and present.
